3º de Primaria · Inglés

Likes and dislikes

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Te encanta la pizza y odias las espinacas. Tu amiga inglesa te pregunta «Do you like spinach?». ¿Qué contestas sin hacer caras raras?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Contestas «No, I don't. I don't like spinach.» Y si quieres decir que algo te encanta: «I love pizza!». Con love, like, don't like y hate puedes decir exactamente cuánto te gusta cada cosa.

2

Aprende15 apartados

Para empezar: Two very different friends

Hugo and Nadia are best friends, but they are very different.

Hugo loves sport. He plays football every day after school, and he likes swimming and riding his bike. He doesn't like reading, and he hates drawing. "It's boring!" he says.

Nadia loves books. She reads every night before bed. She likes painting and playing the piano, and she loves animals. She doesn't like football at all.

At lunchtime, they are different too. Hugo likes pasta and chicken, but he doesn't like vegetables. Nadia loves salad and fruit, but she hates fish.

"So what do you like doing together?" asks Hugo's mum one day.

Hugo and Nadia look at each other and smile.

"We love going to the zoo!" says Nadia.

"And we both like ice cream!" says Hugo. "Chocolate ice cream!"

"Me too!" says Hugo's mum. "Let's go and get some."

Friends don't need to like the same things. They just need to like each other.

1. I like, I don't like

To say what we enjoy, we use I like + thing: «I like apples», «I like football», «I like blue». To say the opposite, use I don't like: «I don't like onions», «I don't like rain».

En castellano: en español decimos «me gusta el chocolate», pero en inglés la persona va delante y el verbo like en medio: «I like chocolate». No digas «me like» ni «to me like». Sin the: «I like dogs», no «I like the dogs».

2. Love and hate

To say it more strongly, use love (encantar) and hate (odiar). We can put all the verbs on a scale: I love ❤️❤️ → I like ❤️ → It's OK → I don't like ✗ → I hate ✗✗.

«I love ice cream! I like fish. I don't like carrots. I hate mushrooms!» Consejo: hate es una palabra muy fuerte; cuando hablas de comida en casa de alguien, es más educado decir «I don't like it very much».

3. Do you like…?

To ask someone, use Do you like…?: «Do you like cats?», «Do you like swimming?». The short answers are: Yes, I do. or No, I don't.

You can add more information: «Yes, I do. I love cats!» or «No, I don't. I prefer dogs.» Ojo: no se contesta «Yes, I like» a secas; la respuesta corta es con do: «Yes, I do».

Vídeo: Do You Like Lasagna Milkshakes? · Super Simple Songs (YouTube) · 1028,9 millones de visualizaciones

4. What… do you like?

With Do you like…? the answer is yes or no. But to get more information, we can ask with What:

  • «What food do you like?» – «I like pizza and strawberries.»
  • «What sports do you like?» – «I like tennis and basketball.»
  • «What animals do you like?» – «I love dolphins.»
  • «What music do you like?» – «I like pop music.»

We can also ask about things we don't like:

  • «What food don't you like?» – «I don't like mushrooms.» (setas)

And to ask why (por qué), use Why? and answer with because (porque):

  • «I don't like spiders.» – «Why?» – «Because they're scary.»
  • «I love summer because there's no school!»

Useful adjectives for reasons: fun (divertido), boring (aburrido), delicious (delicioso), disgusting (asqueroso), scary (que da miedo), cute (mono), exciting (emocionante).

Activity: ask three classmates «What animals do you like? Why?» and write their answers.

5. Food I like

Food is a great topic for likes and dislikes. Fruit: apples, bananas, oranges, strawberries (fresas), grapes (uvas). Vegetables: carrots, tomatoes, peas (guisantes), broccoli. Other food: pizza, pasta, chicken (pollo), fish, eggs, cheese (queso), chips (patatas fritas) and ice cream.

With fruit and vegetables we use the plural: «I like strawberries», «I don't like carrots». But: «I like cheese», «I like fish» (sin -s).

6. Breakfast, lunch and dinner

We eat different things at different meals (comidas):

  • breakfast (desayuno): «For breakfast, I have milk and toast.» Other ideas: cereal, yoghurt, orange juice, an egg.
  • lunch (comida): «For lunch, I have soup, chicken and an apple.»
  • snack (merienda o tentempié): «For my snack, I have a sandwich.»
  • dinner (cena): «For dinner, I have fish and salad.»

Look: in English we say have breakfast, have lunch, have dinner. And «For breakfast, I have…».

Some food is healthy (sano) and we can eat it every day: fruit, vegetables, fish, water, rice, bread, milk. Other food is unhealthy (poco sano) if we eat too much: sweets, crisps (patatas fritas de bolsa), fizzy drinks (refrescos), cakes, burgers.

It's OK to have a treat (capricho) sometimes, but not every day!

In the UK, lunch is often a small meal at about 12 or 1 o'clock, and dinner is the big meal at about 6 or 7 o'clock. In Spain, lunch is usually the big meal of the day, and we have dinner much later.

Activity: write what you have for breakfast, lunch and dinner on a normal day.

Vídeo: Do You Like Pickle Pudding? | Kids Food Song | Super Simple Songs · Super Simple Songs - Kids Songs (YouTube) · 202,9 millones de visualizaciones

7. Activities I like: like + -ing

We can like activities too. After like, love and hate, the verb takes -ing: «I like swimming», «I love dancing», «I don't like running», «I hate getting up early».

Spelling: most verbs just add -ing (play → playing, read → reading). If the verb ends in -e, the e goes away (dance → dancing, ride → riding). Short verbs like swim and run double the last letter: swimming, running.

8. Me too! Me neither!

When a friend tells us what they like, we can agree (estar de acuerdo) or disagree (no estar de acuerdo).

When your friend says something positive:

  • «I like cats.» – «Me too!» (¡Yo también!) if you like cats.
  • «I like cats.» – «Really? I don't.» (¿De verdad? A mí no.) if you don't like cats.

When your friend says something negative:

  • «I don't like spiders.» – «Me neither!» (¡Yo tampoco!) if you don't like them either.
  • «I don't like spiders.» – «Really? I do!» (¿De verdad? ¡A mí sí!) if you like them.

Be careful! After a negative sentence, we don't say Me too. We say Me neither. In Spanish it's the same: yo también / yo tampoco.

It's polite to disagree in a friendly way. We can add: «That's OK. We're different!»

Game: Stand up if… The teacher says: «I love chocolate!» Pupils who agree stand up and say «Me too!». The teacher says: «I don't like rain.» Pupils who agree stand up and say «Me neither!».

Activity: with a partner, say five likes and dislikes and answer with «Me too», «Me neither», «I don't» or «I do».

9. My favourite…

The thing you like the most is your favourite: «My favourite colour is green», «My favourite food is pasta», «My favourite animal is the dolphin». To ask: «What's your favourite sport?» — «It's basketball!»

Ortografía: en inglés británico se escribe favourite y colour con u; en inglés americano, favorite y color. Las dos están bien, pero en el cole solemos usar la británica.

10. He likes, she likes

To talk about another person, we add -s to the verb: «My brother likes football», «She loves horses», «My dad hates spiders». In the negative we use doesn't like: «My sister doesn't like milk».

Questions: «Does your friend like music?» — «Yes, he does.» / «No, she doesn't.» Truco: con he y she, la -s va en el verbo o en el does, pero nunca en los dos: «she doesn't like», no «she doesn't likes».

11. Does he like…?

To ask about another person, we use Does + he / she + like (without -s):

  • «Does your brother like football?» – «Yes, he does.» / «No, he doesn't.»
  • «Does Nadia like fish?» – «No, she doesn't. She hates it.»
  • «Does your cat like milk?» – «Yes, it does.»

Look carefully: the -s goes on does, not on like. We never say Does he likes…?

Compare:

  • Positive: «He likes football.» (with -s)
  • Negative: «He doesn't like football.» (no -s)
  • Question: «Does he like football?» (no -s)

And with What: «What food does your sister like?» – «She likes pasta.»

For two or more people, we use do: «Do your parents like music?» – «Yes, they do.»

Activity: ask a partner about their family: «Does your mum like…? Does your grandpa like…?»

12. Reading: a class survey

Class 3B did a survey (encuesta) about food. Read the results: «Fifteen children like pizza, but three children don't like it. Twelve children love ice cream. Only two children like broccoli! Most children hate onions. Our teacher, Miss Clark, loves fish and she doesn't like chips.»

Answer: How many children like broccoli? Does Miss Clark like chips? What's the favourite food of the class?

13. Our survey in a bar chart

After a survey, we can show the results in a bar chart (gráfico de barras). It helps us see the answers quickly.

How to make it:

  • 1. Choose a question: «What's your favourite fruit?»
  • 2. Give four or five options: apples, bananas, strawberries, oranges, grapes.
  • 3. Ask everybody in the class and make a tally (recuento con palitos): IIII.
  • 4. Draw the bar chart: the fruits at the bottom, the numbers on the side, and one bar for each fruit.

Then write about the results with these phrases:

  • «Most children like strawberries.» (la mayoría)
  • «Ten children like bananas.»
  • «Only two children like grapes.» (solo)
  • «Nobody likes lemons!» (nadie)
  • «Apples are more popular than oranges.»

Remember: nobody and everybody take the verb with -s: «Nobody likes…», «Everybody likes…».

Surveys are also part of Maths: we collect data, count and compare.

Activity: do a survey in your class about favourite sports and draw a bar chart.

14. Let's practise: find your food twin

Make a card with five things: a food, an animal, a sport, a colour and a school subject. Walk around and ask: «Do you like pasta?», «Do you like maths?». Find someone who answers «Yes, I do» to all your questions: that's your food twin (tu gemelo de gustos)!

Then report to the class: «Marta likes pasta and cats. She doesn't like maths. Her favourite colour is purple.» ¿Has encontrado a alguien con los mismos gustos que tú?

15. Write about what you like

Now you can write a text about yourself and your likes and dislikes. Use different verbs, add reasons and join your ideas.

Look at this example:

Hi! I'm Lucas and I'm eight. I love animals, especially horses, because they're beautiful and strong. I like playing basketball with my friends and I like reading comics. I don't like getting up early, and I hate tomatoes! My favourite food is pizza. My sister Ana likes dancing, but she doesn't like sport. And what about you? What do you like?

Tips for a good text:

  • Use different verbs: love, like, don't like, hate.
  • Use -ing with activities: playing, reading, getting up.
  • Add reasons with because.
  • Join ideas with and (y) and but (pero): She likes dancing, but she doesn't like sport.
  • Write about another person with -s: She likes, he loves.
  • Finish with a question to the reader.

Activity: write your own text with at least eight sentences. Read it to the class.

Lo hacemos juntos

Traduce: «Me encantan los perros».

  1. Encantar = love.
  2. La persona va delante: I.
  3. Perros en plural.

Resultado: I love dogs.

Contesta en negativa: «Do you like snakes?»

  1. Respuesta corta con do.
  2. Negativa: don't.

Resultado: No, I don't.

Corrige: «My sister like swim.»

  1. Con she, el verbo lleva -s: likes.
  2. Después de like, verbo con -ing.

Resultado: My sister likes swimming.

Answer «Me too» or «Me neither»: «I don't like rain» (you don't like it either).

  1. The sentence is negative.
  2. To agree with a negative, we say Me neither.

Resultado: Me neither!

Correct: «Does she likes pizza?»

  1. The -s goes on does.
  2. Like has no -s in questions.

Resultado: Does she like pizza?

Errores típicos

  • Traducir palabra por palabra: «Me like» → «I like».
  • Responder «Yes, I like» → «Yes, I do».
  • Olvidar la -s con he o she: «He like» → «He likes».
  • Poner -s dos veces: «She doesn't likes» → «She doesn't like».
  • Olvidar el -ing: «I like swim» → «I like swimming».
  • Saying «Me too» after a negative sentence instead of «Me neither».
  • Writing «Does he likes…?» with two -s.

PracticaResponde sin mirar arriba. Equivocarse aquí también enseña.

Ejercicios (24)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Traduce: me gusta, no me gusta, me encanta, odio.

    Ver solución
    I like, I don't like, I love, I hate.

  2. Pregunta si le gusta el chocolate.

    Ver solución
    Do you like chocolate?

  3. Contesta (sí): «Do you like music?»

    Ver solución
    Yes, I do.

  4. How do you say «desayuno» in English?

    Ver solución
    Breakfast.

  5. Answer: «I like chocolate.» (you like it too)

    Ver solución
    Me too!

  6. Complete: «___ your brother like football?»

    Ver solución
    Does.

  7. Is fruit healthy or unhealthy?

    Ver solución
    Healthy.

  8. In the reading, what does Hugo love?

    Ver solución
    Sport.

Nivel medio

  1. Completa: «I don't ___ carrots.»

    Ver solución
    like.

  2. Escribe con -ing: dance, swim, read.

    Ver solución
    dancing, swimming, reading.

  3. Completa: «My mum ___ (love) flowers.»

    Ver solución
    loves.

  4. Escribe en negativa: «He likes milk.»

    Ver solución
    He doesn't like milk.

  5. Pregunta por su color favorito.

    Ver solución
    What's your favourite colour?

  6. Make a question: What / sports / you / like?

    Ver solución
    What sports do you like?

  7. Answer: Does Nadia like fish?

    Ver solución
    No, she doesn't. She hates fish.

  8. Write a reason: «I like dogs because…»

    Ver solución
    Example: because they're cute and friendly.

  9. Translate: Nadie quiere limones.

    Ver solución
    Nobody likes lemons.

  10. What do you have for breakfast?

    Ver solución
    Example: For breakfast, I have milk and cereal.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Traduce: fresas, guisantes, queso.

    Ver solución
    strawberries, peas, cheese.

  2. Escribe dos cosas que te gustan y una que no.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I love pizza. I like playing football. I don't like onions.

  3. What do Hugo and Nadia both like?

    Ver solución
    They love going to the zoo and they like chocolate ice cream.

  4. Do a survey of five classmates and write three sentences about the results.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  5. Write a text about your likes and dislikes with because, and and but.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  6. Write five questions with Does to ask about a classmate's family.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeClass likes in numbers

The class does surveys about food, sports and animals, makes bar charts and writes a report with the results.

Pasos

  1. Choose a question and four options in groups.
  2. Ask the whole class and make a tally.
  3. Draw a bar chart and write sentences with most, only and nobody.
  4. Present the results and agree or disagree with Me too and Me neither.

Producto final: A wall display of surveys and bar charts in English.

Cómo se valora

  • Asks questions with Do you like…? and What…?
  • Uses Does he like…? correctly.
  • Agrees and disagrees politely.
  • Writes about likes with because, and and but.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Haced en casa una encuesta en inglés: Do you like…? con cinco comidas y apuntad las respuestas.
  • Jugad a adivinar la comida favorita de cada uno con preguntas de sí o no.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Expresión de gustos y preferencias (like, love, hate), preguntas y respuestas cortas con do / does, léxico de comida y aficiones (Lengua Extranjera: Inglés) (RD 157/2022, segundo ciclo de Primaria, 3.er curso).

  • Encuesta de gustos de la clase con gráfico de barras.
  • Juego «Find your food twin».
  • Escala de emociones con caras para love / hate.

Revisado el 22 de noviembre de 2026.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Say what you like and don't like with I like / I don't like
  • Ask «Do you like…?» and answer «Yes, I do / No, I don't»
  • Talk about food, colours and activities you love or hate
  • Use he likes / she likes for other people
  • Ask «What… do you like?» and «Does he like…?»
  • Agree and disagree with «Me too!» and «Me neither!»
  • Talk about meals and healthy food
  • Do a class survey and write about likes and dislikes

Palabras clave

like · don't like · love · hate · Do you like…? · Yes, I do · No, I don't · favourite · likes · doesn't like

Tiempo

80 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
